messages:
Ara Chen: Heads up — after the adaptive-kernel-sampler merge I'm seeing p99 spikes for streamed small responses when continuous batching is enabled. p99 went 220ms -> 420ms on rtx-pool-3, taily behavior around partial-decode steps.

Mike R.: Do you have a repro or a trace? Which route?

Ara Chen: Repro is on the perf harness (small_token_flow). Observations: small token budgets (<=8) + KV cold misses. Profiler shows the kernel selector oscillating mid-request: small_kernel -> large_kernel -> small_kernel. Each switch adds ~1.1-1.4ms plus stalls in the streamer. Example log snippet: 

```
[kernel_selector] req=0x7f pick small_kernel (seq_len=12, batch=6)
[kernel_selector] decision: promote -> large_kernel (reason=batch_size_growth)
[kernel_selector] context switch cost=1.25ms, compile_cache_miss=0
[streamer] partial_decode emitted token_idx=3, prefetch_miss -> kv_warmup
[kernel_selector] request re-eval -> small_kernel (reason: token_budget_conservative)
```

Jin Park: That pattern screams interaction between admission sampler + token_budget_target. We bumped token_budget_target to 32 to reduce tiny batches, but streaming does early-flush on partial-decode which creates micro-batches that trigger re-eval. Two mitigations: pin kernel for the lifetime of a request once first decode starts, or introduce a short sticky window (50ms) after kernel selection to avoid same-request handoffs.

Sasha G: Also note KV warmup. If we early-flush we miss the prefix KV prefetch and then the subsequent micro-batch misses again, causing extra latency. For streaming routes we could bias admission to wait an extra 8-12ms when kv_miss_estimate>0. That is small but reduces repeated misses.

Ara Chen: Proposed experiment: A) toggle sticky_kernel_on_partial_decode=true with sticky_window_ms=100. B) reduce max_batch_window_ms from 60->30 for streaming routes and increase token_budget_target to 48 for small-token flows to avoid frequent kernel upsizing. We'll run the perf harness (2k streamed chats, token sizes 1-8, 50% kv_cold).

Mike R.: SGTM. I'll schedule the tryjob. Please include a comparison of kernel-switch counts and compile_cache_evictions.

Ara Chen: Quick local run results (before -> after sticky kernel): p95 130ms -> 125ms, p99 420ms -> 260ms, kernel_switches/request dropped from 1.8 -> 0.2 on average. Throughput regressed ~3% under synthetic load.

Jin Park: Good delta. Two follow-ups: 1) add idempotency guard in streamer to prevent duplicate emissions when partial decode + handoff reorder happens (we've seen duplicate tokens in canary previously). 2) monitor compile_cache miss rate — frequent kernel switching thrashes JIT/compile cache; if compile_cache_miss > threshold prefer generic/interpreted kernel.

Sasha G: Yep +1. Also add a small metric: kernel_stickiness_ratio and kv_prefetch_hit_rate per route so we can tune per-model.

ops-bot: tryjob/2956789012-run1 started on canary pool.

Mike R.: Canary results: p99 ~200ms (improved), throughput -1.5%. compile_cache_miss reduced by ~40% with sticky kernel. Ops: roll forward to 5% traffic with telemetry flags on, keep sticky_window_ms=100, enable idempotency guard. :thumbsup:

Ara Chen: Will follow up with the tryjob artifact and a perf dashboard link. Thanks team.
